title: Piron, Jim Robinson, Santo Pecora and other New Orleans musicians
summary: Moore recalls A. J. Piron, Jim Robinson, Santo Pecora, Fats Pichon, the Dreamland and Hipe Ginley's, and Jelly Roll Morton whom he will cover later.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, I see. How about A. J. Piron, you played with him for a while? Tell us about -- he was a rather suave individual, wasn't he?

Oh, yeh, played beautiful fiddle. He had a nice little group on Bourbon Street and I had occasion to sit in quite a few times. I worked one night with them. A. J. Piron, I shall never forget him, as well as down the street was Fats Pichon, famous boggie-woggie piano player and also -- I can't think of it right now.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Oh, Jim Robinson was one of the greats also and he played most of the big jazz bands in Preservation Hall and he's one of the greats, I'm telling, Jim Robinson, I loved to hear him play.
Did you hear him play much in New Orleans at that time when you were there, a great deal, Jim Robinson?
Yeah. Since we're talking about trombones, there was another fella there by the name of Santo Pecora.

He's a very good friend of mine. Now, I don't know if he's still in the business but at that time ------ in '39 ------ he was really a wailing -- you know. And there was Hipe Ginley's on Bourbon Street, too. There were some nice bands in there, bands you never heard. They played together and then accept an engagement and then they'd break up again.
That was the name of an establishment? What's the name of it again?
Hipe Ginley, that was the name of a club where all the musicians worked and the Dreamland

was a jumping place. Snookum Russell played the Dreamland by himself on piano.
And Mr. Jelly Roll, did you ever -- well, he was in New York a lot at that time.
Well, he wasn't in New Orleans at that time. Oh, he loved New York. I've got some stories about Jelly Roll I'll cover when my New York segment comes up.
